title.en: Variation and how traits are expressed
Why are siblings alike but not identical?

text.en: Two brothers share the same parents, yet one is taller and has curly hair. Variation arises during reproduction and genes decide how traits show.

Reproduction gives new individuals that are similar to their parents but subtly different. These small differences are called variations.
In asexual reproduction, variation arises only from small inaccuracies in DNA copying. A field of sugarcane shows very little variation.
In sexual reproduction, even greater diversity is created, because DNA from two parents is combined.
Variations build up over generations. Some help the organism survive, for example heat-resistant bacteria in a heat wave. Selection of variants by the environment is the basis of evolution.
Traits are controlled by DNA in the cell. A section of DNA that provides information to make one protein is called a gene.
Proteins act as enzymes and hormones. For example, a plant is tall if its gene makes enough of the hormone for growth, so a less efficient gene gives a shorter plant.
Each cell has two copies of every gene, one from each parent, so each parent contributes equally to the DNA of the child.
The genes are present on separate pieces of DNA called chromosomes. Because they are separate, traits can be inherited independently, giving new combinations.

problem.en: A cell has 2 copies of each gene. If a plant has 6 genes studied, how many gene copies?

why.en: One from each parent for every gene.

prompt.en: Explain why sexual reproduction creates more variation than asexual reproduction.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all children are copies of parents

points.en: Variation arises by DNA copying errors and by combining DNA of two parents.
A gene is a section of DNA that makes a protein.
Each parent gives one copy of each gene.
